handoff.reason: Case report of acute kidney injury and hyperbilirubinemia after Tribulus terrestris ingestion.
Case report of priapism caused by Tribulus terrestris.
2 of 4 cases in a cardiology case series link Tribulus terrestris intake to ventricular fibrillation/aborted sudden cardiac death.
Animal/in vitro mechanistic study finding hepatorenal toxicity of an isolated Tribulus terrestris saponin (Terrestrosin D).
Pharmacovigilance review documents 3 Tribulus terrestris-antidepressant drug interactions (citalopram, escitalopram, trazodone).
Case report of severe liver and renal injury from Tribulus terrestris.
Case report of rhabdomyolysis from a Tribulus terrestris-atorvastatin interaction (proposed CYP3A4 inhibition).
Animal (rat) mechanistic study of Tribulus terrestris nephro/hepatoprotection against carboplatin toxicity.
Trial found significant elevation of aspartate transaminase and total PSA after 3 months of Tribulus terrestris.

identity_notes: Tribulus terrestris evidence splits sharply by indication and, crucially, by whether it is given ALONE or in combination. As a SOLE agent for its two most-marketed claims -- testosterone/androgen enhancement and athletic/strength performance -- the single-ingredient trials are consistently negative (10861339, 15994038, 17530942, 24630840, 27337519, 34836225, 36498228) and a dedicated systematic review concludes 'TT is ineffective for increasing testosterone levels in humans' as a sole agent (24559105); positive testosterone findings only appear when tribulus is combined with other ingredients, and the contributing component cannot be isolated. For FEMALE sexual dysfunction (desire/arousal), sole-agent tribulus trials are more consistently positive (24773615, 26902700, 27760089, 29172782, 34142638) and a meta-analysis (34638031) and systematic review (32736394) both report positive pooled effects, though certainty of evidence is graded very low. For MALE erectile dysfunction, results are decidedly mixed: some sole-agent trials are positive (28364864, large n=180) while others are negative (24630840) or of low evidence quality (40219032); most other 'ED' evidence in this scope involves tribulus as one ingredient in a combination product (Tradamixina, Tradamix, Icarifil, ginseng+tribulus+L-arginine, etc.) and should not be credited to tribulus alone -- these are flagged related_form_differs/combination throughout. A distinct and clinically important SAFETY signal cluster exists: multiple case reports of acute kidney injury, priapism, ventricular fibrillation, and severe liver/renal injury attributed to tribulus supplements, plus a documented CYP3A4-mediated rhabdomyolysis interaction with atorvastatin and 3 antidepressant interactions -- all routed to handoff. One trial (30253697) also found significant elevations in AST and PSA after 3 months of use, a hepatic/prostate safety signal worth flagging alongside the case reports.
